methodology: The decree table explicitly distinguishes the administrative imada column from the electoral circle column. Each accepted identity was visually located under the correct delegation, rather than assumed equivalent from matching names or numeric codes.
Whole-imada conclusion requires a direct one-imada to one-circle row. A parent with fewer than5imadas can still contain whole-imada circles; it is not by itself an exclusion rule.
The map PDF title/parent and current INS identity had already been independently cross-checked; this adds the missing legal semantic check. No polygon unions, splits or edits were performed.
Arabic text is visually transcribed; spacing around numerals, hyphens and parentheses is normalized for legibility. It is not an OCR byte-for-byte transcription.

notes: These are the2023 minutes figures, not the later2082-row INS2024 publication count.

The minutes say236delegations have more than5imadas; this wording should not be silently treated as a strict exhaustive mathematical classification because many have exactly5. The43under-five and131exception figures are independently consistent with the decree.
The supplemental43-name list is computed from the three-workbook INS2024 registry. It is useful screening context, not a substitute for inspecting each2023 circle composition.

limitations: This report checks territorial unit semantics in the2023 decree, not survey accuracy, topology against neighboring mixed-source polygons or post2023 legal changes.
Approval applies only to these exact record IDs, official codes and boundarySourceSha256 values. New source records require their own direct semantic review.
